chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman leading the women, so he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.تَؤُمُّ: leads in prayer (female form of imamate)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a woman lead other women in congregational prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the permissibility of a woman leading other women in prayer, reflecting the consensus among Shia jurists that she holds the status of an imam for them. The narration, transmitted through the reliable chain of Sama'ah ibn Mihran, underscores the practical application of female leadership in communal worship within the domestic or private sphere, distinct from the male-led congregational prayers.
